annotations.text:
Sésame — four directions for the look & feel.

Same screen, same copy, four aesthetics. Pick one and I'll build it into the real app.

Each has a different bet about the reader: someone anxious, often reading their second or third language, usually in a hurry.

A · WARM EDITORIAL — reads like a good guidebook. Serif headline, ruled sections, warm paper.
Bet: calm and authority come from restraint. Best legibility for long answers.
Tradeoff: quiet. Less memorable at a glance than B or D.

B · CIVIC BOLD — Swiss signage. Heavy type, flat colour blocks, hard edges, no shadows.
Bet: newcomers scan before they read, so shout the structure. Strongest at a glance and in translation.
Tradeoff: loud. Can read as institutional — the very thing the reader is anxious about.

C · SOFT & CALM — rounded, airy, gentle indigo. Centred, generous, low-pressure.
Bet: the emotional problem is fear, so lower the temperature.
Tradeoff: the most conventional of the four. Closest to the current design, and to every other app.

D · PAPER & STAMP — kraft paper, stamp red, monospace metadata, dossier framing.
Bet: lean into the subject. Makes officialdom feel handled rather than hostile.
Tradeoff: the most opinionated. Charm could read as flippant about something people are genuinely worried about.
